content: I had a lot of Claude usage left, so I thought I could use them to do something very tedious in mathlib that I’ve always wanted to do: fixing inconsistencies of declarations including typos and porting mistakes from Lean 3. I asked Claude to scan through just the declarations in mathlib and gather all that it thinks is inconsistent. I hope this isn’t intrusive and does not break any community laws, and hopefully the PRs are not too hard to review. A very early starting point is #43889 which doesn’t have deprecations added yet, because I’d like to see what people think before I continue further.
I’ve just looked at all of them manually and urgh, I can’t believe these went through! Anyways they all seem fine except for the alternization thing which I don’t know about

I (Claude) have added something in the PR description
If you enforce that I should change at most 10 files max per PR, then Claude tells me there are something like ~500 typo PRs to be made :)
You can also classify by looking at the same typo from different files
Yeah, I can classify the type of typo, but some of them easily modify over 100 files, and I don't want to make reviewers go insane
Another option is separating PRs by module maybe

Pepa Montero Jimena said:

Another option is separating PRs by module maybe

I'm not sure how to do that! I guess I don't understand the module system at all...
"module (name)" = "file (name)"

Anyways, this PR seems to be hanging around for a bit, presumably because reviewing a PR modifying 60+ files is annoying no matter how easy it is. I could autogenerate about 600 PRs right now fixing docstring/comment typos rather than declarations, marking each of them as "easy". Would people prefer that? Would each of them get merged quickly so as to keep the queue as short as before?
I could separate them by files, but that would make reviewing slightly harder, because the changes are slightly different in each file
I definitely wouldn't create 600 PRs all at once, because it will clutter the PR list on github.
Yeah that makes sense :laughter_tears: but I can do a few everyday. Maybe a maintainer is willing to have a look and merge things within a minute each PR.

I think typos in declaration names are a lot more important to fix than typos in docstrings/comments. Maybe you could split your first PR into a few parts. And then we can think about what we want to do with all the other typos, and how to best classify them for easier review. I would think that splitting based on the kind of typo would make review easiest (e.g. if the same typo appears in many places, then that can be one PR)
You can have a look at https://github.com/Multramate/mathlib4/blob/claude/comment-audit/docs/typos.md

Ooh, cool! I looked at a few of the categories, and it looks like there are quite some false positives (i.e. things that were done intentionally rather than accidentally). But if a category of typos doesn't have false positives, then it would probably make for an easy PR.

With my maintainer hat on, but my personal opinion:

  • we want to fix these misnamed declarations for sure, and PRs correcting this are appreciated
  • when you rename a declaration, updating comment references is also appreciated. (Moving to verso docstrings will require this, so this is work that should happen regardless.)
  • grouping by kind of typo is good as it makes review easier (and for these kind of PRs, we really want to make reviewers' job easier!)
  • it's good to throttle the PR rate to a reasonable number. Having 3-5 open PRs at the same time seems fine to me, more feels like too much.
Thanks for investigating this and being willing to help fix this!
Great! In this case I will split #43889 to a few for now.
This is now #44049, #44050, #44051, #44052, and I'll close #43889 if this split is good.
All of them has been merged, thanks! The next round of PRs are #44290 #44291 #44292 #44296
I noticed (not in these PRs) that there is a bunch of coe_fn_* and coe_fun_* --- the role of fn/fun here is mostly non-existent?
(I violated Kevin's rule that a PR shouldn't change more than 10 files, but I hope the not_mem -> notMem change is fine...)

See #mathlib4 > Convention for `f * g` and / or `fun x ↦ f x * g x` @ 💬 for fn/fun. It should be fun when the statement has a fun _ ↦ ..., fn is probably wrong (or old). There's also a @[to_fun] attribute to autogenerate some of these btw.
I think coe_fn/coe_fun is about coercions to functions (⇑), e.g. from A →* B to A → B
In that case those should only say coe, referring to docs#DFunLike.coe
There is also coeFn

That seems wrong, but it depends on where. There are a few coeFn definitions (e.g. docs#MonoidHom.coeFn), which aren't registered as coercions, so a theorem should be named coeFn only when the statement includes it.
docs#ContinuousLinearMap.range_coeFn_eq seems strange, perhaps DFunLike.coe used to be called coeFn and was renamed? (edit: this specific example is rather new, but others are from before FunLike was introduced and coercions of functions were just referred to as "coe fn")

For coercions I believe the convention is to hover the arrow and see what coercion function it uses, then name it after that.
e.g. docs#Function.Embedding.coeFn_mk and docs#RelHom.coeFn_mk should use coe, but docs#MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.liftRel_iff_coeFn and docs#MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.coeFn_le should use cast (referring to docs#MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.cast)
For now I won't touch this coeFn issue, but instead here is four more #44326 #44327 #44328 #44329 since the previous four are merged :)
Ehh I'm not too convinced with the name choice of #44329 but maybe changing preserves_(co)limit to another name is still valid
The next 4 are #44519 #44520 #44521 #44522 since 3/4 of the previous ones got merged
The next 4 are #44641 #44642 #44643 #44645 since all 4 of the previous ones got merged (with #44328 still from the previous week)
The next 4 are #44823 #44824 #44825 #44826 since all 4 of the previous ones got merged (with #44328 still from two weeks ago)

The first of these PRs should (hopefully) fix all the remaining declarations with typos. The other three are arguably also misdeclarations, but not necessarily typos. For instance, there are 1500+ instances of ne_zero but only <100 instances of nonzero, so I think it's worth the change.
